$comment: What was read, and at which revision, for every column of the comparison table in README.md.
The table is the one thing this project ships that makes claims about other people's software,
and it goes wrong without anything breaking. `npm run smoke` already checks how OLD it is;
this file makes it checkable whether the other side has MOVED since we looked, which is the
question that actually decides whether a cell still holds. `npm run table-sources` compares
each `sha` against that project's current HEAD and names the columns worth re-reading.
Adopted from csitte.at, whose rule is 'no matrix cell without our own evidence' — they record
the foreign HEAD before mirroring a row. On 2026-08-26 their recorded SHA for taylorwilsdon
and ours matched, which is how a claim about a third party should be confirmable at all.
`shaBasis` is deliberately part of the record: `recorded` means the SHA was read at the time
of checking, `inferred` means it was reconstructed afterwards from the commit history (safe
only when the repository did not move between the check and the reconstruction). Never write
`recorded` for a SHA nobody wrote down — that is the exact habit this file exists to break.

columns.note: Full re-read of the MCP tool reference itself on 2026-09-03 (not the Cloud blog), replacing the 2026-08-31 reading of the same page: still Developer Preview, and the same ten tools by name — create_draft, get_message, get_thread, label_message, label_thread, list_drafts, list_labels, search_threads, unlabel_message, unlabel_thread. No send, no filters, no unsubscribe, no snooze, no query-driven bulk. The page documents no return fields at all, which is why the structured-output and sender-authentication cells both read as not offered / not documented rather than as a denial: nothing there mentions SPF, DKIM, DMARC or Authentication-Results. Every cell in this column checked against that page, not carried over.

Full re-read of all eleven cells on 2026-08-31 at this revision (the 2026-08-29 entry was a delta check; this replaces it). Read gmail/gmail_tools.py end to end: sixteen Gmail tools, send_gmail_message present, no snooze, no unsubscribe action (List-Unsubscribe only appended to the exported message body), search_gmail_messages returns ids and links without re-checking labels, batch_modify_gmail_message_labels takes message_ids — an explicit list, not a query — and defaults verify=True, which reads the labels back. auth/credential_store.py CHANGED A CELL: LocalDirectoryCredentialStore writes with file mode 0600 and no encryption, GCSCredentialStore delegates to bucket-level CMEK with 'no app-level key'. The cell said a plain yes, which read as app-level token encryption like ours; now it names both mechanisms. No output_schema anywhere in the repository. Scope coupling unchanged since 2026-08-26 (auth/scopes.py, main.py). He now also sells a managed instance, which does not change the 'you operate the server' row: self-hosting remains fully supported. 2026-09-03: brought forward from the 2026-08-31 revision by reading the diff rather than the files again — eleven commits, and none of them touches a cell. They are an OAuth client-secret-file fallback (auth/client_secrets.py, auth/oauth_config.py, core/server.py, main.py) and label colours on the existing manage_gmail_label tool (gmail/gmail_tools.py, gmail/gmail_helpers.py); the tool count, the scope model, the storage mechanisms and the absence of output_schema are all untouched. The sender-authentication cell was re-checked at this HEAD directly: GMAIL_METADATA_HEADERS still ends at List-Id (lines 42-44, which is also the control that proves the search works), and Authentication-Results, dkim, dmarc and spf have no hit in the file. A diff that leaves a cell's code identical is a stronger record than reading the same lines twice — but it is a different check, and this note says which one was run.
